items.title: Quad unveils security, business, AI plans; Trump offers open line
items.where: Front page lead, continued on page 2 (Shubhajit Roy)
items.syllabus: GS2 › Bilateral, regional and global groupings involving India and/or affecting India's interests · GS3 › Security challenges in maritime areas; cyber security; science and technology (AI) · GS4 › Ethics in international relations
items.summary: At their first leaders' meeting since 2024, on the EAS sidelines in Manila, the Quad announced a maritime surveillance collaboration, an AI accelerator, enhanced cyber cooperation, critical mineral deals and a Business Leaders' Forum in Mumbai in 2027.
evolution: Last Quad leaders' meeting before Manila.
Manila meeting: maritime surveillance, AI, cyber, critical minerals and a business forum; joint statement condemns cross-border terrorism.
ideas: Security core deepens: P-8 and P-3C aircraft to fly a first Quad maritime exercise in 2027; Malabar already drills anti-submarine warfare.
GS2 · Indo-Pacific / GS3 · Maritime security
The Quad is moving from dialogue to joint operations at sea.
Beyond security: AI accelerator, cyber cooperation, critical minerals and a Business Leaders' Forum (Mumbai, 2027).
GS2 · Groupings / GS3 · Technology
The Quad now delivers trusted technology and supply chains, not just patrols.
Joint statement opposes changing the status quo by force or coercion, and economic coercion through arbitrary export restrictions.
GS2 · Rules-based order
The Quad's message: no change by force, no leverage through supply chains.
Condemns cross-border terrorism; Modi calls the Quad 'a constructive and trusted partnership'.
GS2 · India's interests / GS3 · Terrorism
The Quad also carries India's concern on cross-border terror.
keywords: Knowing in real time what moves at sea, through shared surveillance and data
The Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration builds shared maritime domain awareness across the Quad.
Using trade, export curbs or supply dependence to force political outcomes
Quad critical mineral deals aim to end vulnerability to economic coercion by any single supplier.
Diversifying sources so no single country can choke supplies
Critical mineral partnerships are about supply-chain resilience, not just trade.
Small, issue-based groupings of like-minded countries
The Quad shows minilateralism: four countries, many issues, no treaty.
examples: Quad navies' anti-submarine and anti-surface drills
Malabar exercise: Quad navies' anti-submarine and anti-surface drills.
Quad Business Leaders' Forum, Mumbai 2027: Quad's economic turn.
trusted AI access for the Indo-Pacific
Quad AI accelerator: trusted AI access for the Indo-Pacific.
pyqs: Quad: from military alliance to trade bloc?
IPMDA: bridge between SAGAR and the Quad's Indo-Pacific strategy.
AUKUS and existing partnerships in the Indo-Pacific.
Geopolitical significance of the South China Sea.
South China Sea, freedom of navigation and India–China issues.
Cross-border cyber attacks and defensive measures.
Ethics subjugated to strategic interests in international relations.

trend.t: Indo-Pacific questions began with the South China Sea and freedom of navigation (2014, 2016), moved to the Quad's own character (2020) and rival groupings such as AUKUS (2021), and in 2026 reached a specific Quad initiative, IPMDA, tested against India's SAGAR vision.
trend.watch: The Quad has been asked directly in 2020 and 2026, and the 2026 question picked one initiative and asked for a critical assessment, so the new surveillance collaboration, AI accelerator or critical minerals deals are the next likely angles.
focus: Quad's shift from security to technology, supply chains and economy
Maritime domain awareness: IPMDA and the 2027 surveillance exercise
India's strategic autonomy within the Quad

potential: "The Quad is evolving from a maritime security dialogue into a partnership for technology, supply chains and economic security." Discuss. (15 marks)
Examine the significance of the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration for India's maritime security. (10 marks)
"Critical minerals have become the new frontier of strategic partnerships." Discuss with reference to the Quad. (10 marks)

practice.q: "The Quad is evolving from a maritime security dialogue into a partnership for technology, supply chains and economic security." Discuss.

answer.t: Started in 2007 and revived in 2017, the Quad met at leaders' level in Manila in November 2026 and announced plans spanning maritime surveillance, AI, cyber security, critical minerals and business.

pts.t: Shared surveillance gives the Indo-Pacific a common picture of what moves at sea, from dark shipping to illegal fishing.
pts.ex: Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration; P-8 and P-3C aircraft in a first Quad exercise in 2027.

pts.t: Regular drills let four navies operate together in anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare.
pts.ex: The 30th Malabar exercise near Japan.

pts.t: The Quad defends open sea lanes and overflight under international law.
pts.ex: Joint statement: 'open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors'.

pts.t: It rejects unilateral changes to the status quo by force or coercion.
pts.ex: Joint statement on destabilising actions that escalate tensions.

pts.t: The grouping condemns terrorism in all forms, including cross-border terrorism.
pts.ex: A key gain for India given terror from across its western border.

pts.t: Disaster response gives the Quad a non-military face in the region.
pts.ex: Modi lists disaster response among the Quad's core areas.

pts.t: The Quad funds trusted AI access and deployment so the region does not depend on untrusted systems.
pts.ex: Quad AI accelerator to coordinate and fund trusted AI across the Indo-Pacific.

pts.t: Rising cyber incidents need shared standards and response.
pts.ex: Enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation for 'an open and secure cyberspace'.

pts.t: New deals diversify supply so no member is vulnerable to a single supplier.
pts.ex: Statement's concern over economic coercion through arbitrary export restrictions.

pts.t: Business ties turn diplomatic intent into investment and jobs.
pts.ex: Inaugural Quad Business Leaders' Forum in Mumbai, 2027.

pts.t: Deliverables for smaller states build legitimacy beyond the four members.
pts.ex: Modi: 'trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific'.

pts.t: Supply chains are now treated as a security question.
pts.ex: MEA: cooperation in maritime security, economic security and critical technologies.

pts.t: The Quad is a loose partnership; commitments depend on political will.
pts.ex: Leaders met in Manila for the first time since 2024.

pts.t: Members differ in how far they want to confront China, given deep trade ties.
pts.ex: The Quad meets just before Trump's trilateral with Xi and Putin.

pts.t: India avoids any alliance commitment and keeps ties with Russia.
pts.ex: India's stand of independent foreign policy and multi-alignment.

pts.t: Shifts in US trade and alliance policy can strain partners.
pts.ex: US tariffs on Indian goods in 2025 tested India–US ties.

pts.t: South-East Asian states fear great-power rivalry eclipsing ASEAN centrality.
pts.ex: Modi's own stress on ASEAN unity and centrality at the EAS.

pts.t: Announcements can outrun implementation and funding.
pts.ex: Critics' 'Asian NATO' framing feeds Chinese pushback if delivery lags.

pts.t: Annual leaders' meetings and a light coordination mechanism keep momentum.
pts.ex: A two-year gap before Manila shows the cost of irregular meetings.

pts.t: Prioritise HADR, health, connectivity and training for smaller states.
pts.ex: Quad Vaccine Partnership as an earlier model.

pts.t: Anchor Quad plans in ASEAN-led platforms such as the EAS.
pts.ex: India's Act East Policy and IPOI.

pts.t: Shape norms for trusted, safe and human-centric technology.
pts.ex: India's AI Impact Summit stress on safe, inclusive AI.

pts.t: Joint processing and stockpiling of critical minerals, not just purchase deals.
pts.ex: Quad critical mineral deals announced in Manila.

pts.t: Present the Quad as a provider of public goods, not a military bloc.
pts.ex: Joint statement: 'a force for good and a partnership of action'.

answer.t: From Malabar drills to an AI accelerator and a Mumbai business forum, the Quad is widening its agenda, and its credibility now rests on delivery to the Indo-Pacific.

items.title: East Asia meet: Modi announces safety initiative for seafarers, flags cyber fraud
items.where: Front page, continued on page 2 (Shubhajit Roy)
items.syllabus: GS2 › Regional groupings (ASEAN, EAS); India's foreign policy (Act East) · GS3 › Security challenges in maritime areas; cyber crime · GS4 › Ethics in international relations
items.summary: At the EAS in Manila, Modi launched a seafarers' safety initiative and proposed an EAS Cyber Crime Conference at NFSU; at the ASEAN-India summit he proposed a long-term maritime cooperation plan, free e-visas for ASEAN tourists and cooperation on critical minerals.
evolution: ADMM-Plus, Cebu: Rajnath offers counter-terror expertise to ASEAN.
G20 foreign ministers: Jaishankar speaks for seafarers and freedom of navigation.
Navy frees hijacked vessel Azini off Somalia.
EAS: seafarers' safety initiative; ASEAN-India: long-term maritime cooperation plan.
ideas: Seafarers' safety initiative: joint training and emergency response, as ships with Indians on board are attacked in Hormuz and the Black Sea.
GS3 · Maritime security / GS2 · EAS
'Our seas are the lifelines of our shared prosperity.'
Cyber fraud and online scams named as new cross-border crime; India offers an EAS Cyber Crime Conference at NFSU.
GS3 · Cyber crime
Cyber fraud is the new cross-border crime.
Act East beyond culture: maritime plan, e-visas, cyber forensics training, critical minerals; 'ASEAN unity and centrality' at its heart.
GS2 · Act East Policy
From shared heritage to digital, defence and space.
keywords: ASEAN-led forums as the core of the region's architecture
India keeps ASEAN centrality at the heart of its Act East Policy.
Crew who keep global trade moving and bear the risk of conflict at sea
Attacks on ships in Hormuz make seafarers frontline workers of global trade.
Tagging AI-made content to fight deepfakes and misinformation
Digital watermarking helps the state counter deepfakes without banning AI.
data: Share of the world's population in India and ASEAN together
India and ASEAN together are nearly a quarter of humanity, PM Modi said at the ASEAN-India Summit.
India's people-to-people outreach to ASEAN since 2014
Since 2014 India has run over 100 people-to-people initiatives and 10,000 skill scholarships for ASEAN, said PM Modi.
examples: joint training and emergency response at sea
GS3 · Maritime security · GS4 · Duty of care
Seafarers' safety initiative (EAS, 2026): joint training and emergency response at sea.
EAS Cyber Crime Conference at NFSU
India's offer on cross-border cyber fraud
EAS Cyber Crime Conference at NFSU: India's offer on cross-border cyber fraud.
Free e-visas for ASEAN tourists: people-to-people connect under Act East.
pyqs: Economic and strategic dimensions of the Look East Policy.
Maritime security and India's sea trade.
IMO's role in maritime safety and security.

trend.t: South-East Asia was asked through the Look East Policy (2016) and the diaspora (2017); maritime security moved from piracy (2014) to initiatives (2022), the IMO (2023) and sea trade (2025).
trend.watch: Maritime security has been asked in 2022, 2023 and 2025, so seafarers' safety and the security of sea lanes is a must-study area; Act East has not been asked directly since 2016 and is due.
focus: Security of sea lanes and seafarers
India–ASEAN in critical minerals and digital

potential: "India's Act East Policy has moved beyond shared culture to maritime, digital and economic security." Discuss. (15 marks)
Why has the safety of seafarers become a maritime security concern for India? Suggest measures. (10 marks)

items.title: On talks table: Multi-skilling, tech proficiency for 6-year Agniveers
items.where: Front page Express Special, continued on page 2 (Amrita Nayak Dutta)
items.syllabus: GS3 › Various security forces and agencies and their mandate · GS2 › Government policies and interventions; skilling and employment of youth · GS1 › Role of women · GS4 › Objectivity and fairness; discipline
items.summary: Under the revamped Agnipath scheme, the 75% of Agniveers not absorbed after four years will get a two-year extension; HQ IDS is deliberating stringent criteria for absorbing them, favouring multi-skilled, tech-proficient soldiers.
evolution: 25% of Agniveers absorbed on merit after four years; the rest exit with a contributory package.
Revamp: the other 75% offered a two-year extension, then a chance to join as regular soldiers on objective criteria.
ideas: Two stages: 25% absorbed after four years; the other 75% get two more years and a second chance at the regular cadre.
GS3 · Security forces
The revamp turns a four-year exit into a six-year pathway.
Preference for multi-skilled Agniveers proficient in technology and weapons, as new systems are inducted.
GS3 · Defence modernisation
Modern weapons need tech-ready soldiers.
Fitness and discipline filters: excellent in physical tests, first-class shot, no Low Medical Category, clean disciplinary record.
GS3 · Combat readiness / GS4 · Discipline
A younger, fitter force is the scheme's core aim.
Objective merit list from unit-level exams and firing tests; a four-option certificate lets each Agniveer state his choice.
GS2 · Policy design / GS4 · Fairness
Objective criteria make selection fair and transparent.
keywords: Lowering the average age of soldiers for combat readiness
Agnipath aims at a youthful profile of the armed forces.
Combat shaped by drones, sensors and advanced weapon systems
Tech-intensive warfare puts a premium on multi-skilled soldiers.
Choosing by measurable criteria, not discretion
Objective selection criteria build trust in Agnipath's merit list.
examples: GS1 · Women in armed forces · GS4 · Gender equality
INS Chilka passing-out: 2,700+ Agniveers, including 142 women, completed training.
a reason for the LMC filter
Lifestyle diseases among troops: a reason for the LMC filter.
pyqs: Demographic dividend needs a skilled, employable population.
'Earn while you learn' and vocational skilling.
Border threats and the role of security forces.
Discipline: order and subordination, yet counterproductive?

trend.t: Agnipath itself has not been asked. Security forces appear through their role in border and internal security (2020), and skilling of youth through the demographic dividend (2016) and 'earn while you learn' (2021).
trend.watch: Defence reform has not been asked directly, so the scheme is best used as an example in answers on security forces, youth employment and skilling.
focus: Skilling and second careers for youth

potential: "Defence manpower reform must balance a youthful, tech-ready force with fairness and career security for soldiers." Discuss with reference to the revamped Agnipath scheme. (15 marks)
How can short-service schemes in the armed forces contribute to skilling India's youth? (10 marks)

ethics.title: Rules, not force: the Quad's stated ethic
ethics.news: Quad leaders opposed any change to the status quo by force or coercion, and economic coercion through arbitrary export restrictions.
ethics.syllabus: Ethics in international relations; rule of law
ethics.link: Opposing coercion, by arms or by trade, applies the rule of law between nations: small states should not be forced by larger ones. Whether the Quad itself stays a provider of public goods, and not a bloc serving only its members' strategic interests, is the ethical test.
ethics.question: "A rules-based order is the ethical alternative to power politics." Discuss with reference to the Quad's stand against coercion in the Indo-Pacific.

ethics.title: Those who keep trade moving: the seafarers
ethics.news: With ships carrying Indian crew attacked in Hormuz and the Black Sea, India launched a seafarers' safety initiative at the East Asia Summit.
ethics.syllabus: Ethics in international relations; compassion; duty of care
ethics.link: Global trade rests on seafarers who bear the cost of conflicts they have no part in. A state that protects its workers abroad shows a duty of care, and making it a shared EAS initiative turns national concern into collective responsibility.
ethics.question: "The safety of those who keep the world's trade moving is a shared moral responsibility." Discuss with reference to attacks on merchant ships.

ethics.title: Merit, fitness and fairness in the Agnipath merit list
ethics.news: HQ IDS is deliberating objective criteria for absorbing Agniveers after six years: fitness, firing standards, disciplinary record and a unit-level merit test.
ethics.syllabus: Objectivity; fairness; discipline in public service
ethics.link: Clear, measurable criteria protect fairness when only some can be absorbed. But fairness also asks for compassion: the possible exception for battle casualties and service-related disabilities recognises that those injured in duty should not lose out.
ethics.question: "Objectivity in selection must be tempered with compassion for those injured in service." Discuss with reference to the revamped Agnipath scheme.
